title: A deleted site's name can be built again, and a press refused TAKEN leaves no site row or seat behind
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout, with TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a scratch PostgreSQL, run: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/site-creation.test.mjs
S2: Record the exit code and the cases named under expect.
expect: A site built, then deleted through DELETE /api/sites/:key (its provision job stays on record), is built again under the same name by the same owner and by another account, with a buildId and without one: 202, a new job id (never the deleted site's job handed back as reused), one site row, one owner seat.
A press refused 409 TAKEN on a live site (by its owner with a new build, and by a stranger) changes neither the site nor the seat count and calls no provision.
An imported domain deleted and imported again gets a new provision, not the deleted copy's job.
evidence: Measured on dev 09/10/2026 21:18 UTC: POST /api/sites for e2e-em (deleted earlier) answered 409 TAKEN and left a site row and owner seat with no job and no container; cms-log-pull failed every minute.
fence: Jobs outlive their site; only jobs filed since the standing row was written count, and the TAKEN test runs before the claim under the provision lock.

tests: a deleted site's name can be built again by the same owner (keyed press)
a deleted site's name can be built again by the same owner (legacy press)
a deleted site's name can be built again by another account (keyed press)
a deleted site's name can be built again by another account (legacy press)
a press refused TAKEN on a live site writes nothing: no site row, no seat, no provision
an imported domain whose site was deleted is imported again, not handed the deleted site's job
